bad_deployment.description: A changed binary introduces errors or latency on its observed request path.
confirming_evidence_patterns: Version or rollout event precedes a sustained symptom increase in the changed service
New-version requests fail while comparable old-version requests remain healthy
contradicting_evidence_patterns: Symptoms precede the deployment
Changed service is absent from affected request paths
Both versions fail with the same downstream error
relevant_trace_patterns: New failed span in changed service
Latency change on the same operation after version transition
typical_red_herrings: Healthy service deployment outside the request path
safe_remediation_suggestions: Propose rollback_deployment only to an explicitly observed prior version; require approval and compatibility checks
verification_conditions: Sustained error-rate and latency return toward baseline across multiple observations
No new failures in caller or dependency services

config_change.description: A runtime configuration or feature flag changes service behavior without requiring a binary deployment.
confirming_evidence_patterns: Named flag/config transition precedes matching code-path errors
Affected cohorts or operations exercise the changed configuration
contradicting_evidence_patterns: Errors occur before the config change
Evidence shows the flag was disabled throughout failures
Unchanged cohorts fail equally with a shared dependency error
required_signals: Observed config key and value transition
relevant_trace_patterns: Changed operation or downstream call only on the affected path
typical_red_herrings: A noisy deploy with no matching changed behavior
safe_remediation_suggestions: Propose revert_config with the observed key and documented prior value; flag disable is a config revert only when actual evidence supports it
verification_conditions: Confirm intended config in simulated state
Observe multiple healthy intervals on previously affected operations

resource_exhaustion.description: CPU, memory, storage, queues, or worker capacity becomes a service bottleneck.
confirming_evidence_patterns: CPU throttling or sustained saturation precedes latency
Memory growth precedes OOM and restarts
Queue growth correlates with request volume beyond available capacity
contradicting_evidence_patterns: Resource use is stable near baseline during failures
Resource spike follows dependency timeouts rather than precedes them
Pressure persists despite traffic falling, contradicting a pure load explanation
required_signals: Resource metric or explicit exhaustion event
Traffic and restart evidence where available
relevant_trace_patterns: Long local execution spans across operations
typical_red_herrings: High CPU on a node outside the affected path
Short resource spikes without correlated symptoms
safe_remediation_suggestions: Propose scale_service only with observed target capacity and known limits
Propose restart_service only for a supported stuck/leaking instance with interruption risk disclosed
verification_conditions: Sustained headroom and reduced queue depth

dependency_failure.description: A failed downstream service propagates errors or delays through observed callers.
confirming_evidence_patterns: Failed downstream spans precede caller timeout/retry logs
Caller-to-failing-service edge appears in affected traces
Downstream latency accounts for the observed request delay
contradicting_evidence_patterns: Dependency calls succeed during caller failures
Alleged dependency is absent from affected request paths
Caller fails before invoking the dependency
required_signals: Failed span or downstream failure signal
relevant_trace_patterns: Slow span on the actual request branch
typical_red_herrings: Caller resource pressure caused by waiting on the dependency
safe_remediation_suggestions: Recommend action only on an evidence-supported failing target; revert observed harmful changes before considering restart or scaling
verification_conditions: Dependency spans recover across multiple requests
Direct and indirect callers show sustained error/latency improvement

database_issue.description: Connection limits, pooling, slow queries, or lock contention disrupt database-backed operations.
confirming_evidence_patterns: Active connections approach an observed maximum before application timeouts
Connection pool saturation precedes failed queries
Lock waits or query latency increase before affected database spans fail
contradicting_evidence_patterns: Database spans and query latency remain healthy while the application fails earlier
Connection usage is well below a known limit
Application errors precede database pressure
required_signals: Database error or failed query span
relevant_trace_patterns: Database child span dominating request duration
typical_red_herrings: High connection count without known capacity
safe_remediation_suggestions: Revert a demonstrated harmful pool/query config change with approval
Do not recommend database restart or capacity changes without supported limits, persistence and impact information
verification_conditions: Multiple observations show healthy query latency and connection headroom where measurable
Application database spans and caller error rates recover without new lock failures

network_issue.description: Connectivity, name resolution, packet loss, or transport problems interrupt observed service communication.
confirming_evidence_patterns: DNS lookup failures or connection resets precede failed remote spans
Independent callers to the same network endpoint fail
Infra events align with affected nodes and request-path edges
contradicting_evidence_patterns: Transport connects successfully and a remote application returns a specific business error
Failures are limited to one changed application code path
Alleged affected node is not hosting any involved pod
relevant_trace_patterns: Connection setup timeout before remote execution
Multiple branches to the same endpoint fail
typical_red_herrings: Generic application timeouts without network evidence
safe_remediation_suggestions: Revert an observed routing/DNS config change only when the exact prior value is available
Escalate unsupported network operations; do not invent a registered repair tool
verification_conditions: Repeated connections and name resolution succeed
Previously affected request paths sustain baseline-like latency/error rates

third_party_degradation.description: An explicitly identified external provider degrades and affects dependent application operations.
confirming_evidence_patterns: External provider spans show latency, throttling, or server errors before local symptoms
Local services remain healthy outside provider-dependent operations
Independent observed provider incident corroborates local trace failures
contradicting_evidence_patterns: External provider returns successful low-latency responses
Local failure happens before the external call
No evidence identifies the dependency as external
relevant_trace_patterns: Slow/failed external child span on the affected operation
typical_red_herrings: Assuming every unfamiliar service is third-party
Local pool exhaustion caused by retry amplification
safe_remediation_suggestions: Revert an evidenced retry/timeout config regression with approval
Suggest provider escalation if no registered action is supported; do not pretend to repair the provider
verification_conditions: Sustained successful provider calls across multiple observations
Caller latency/error rates and retry amplification improve
